secondary_findings.statement: In letters to Titus a numerical cipher was used alongside the letter codes: lower numbers reserved for single letters; two alphabetically-ordered word/syllable series 103(am)-420(you) and 453(business)-608(trouble); numerals 634(one), 647(twenty); days/months 659(Monday), 665(Sunday), 672(May); 680(wife), 686(escape), 705(boat).

secondary_findings.relevance: Same-cipher-family cribs; RP 9319 likely contains figure-name lists in the letters themselves

King sent 'an addition of some Figures, with Names' 26 July 1648.

records_examined.contents_note: Item 5: letter to Firebrace enclosing a letter from the king, 'On the back is a cipher of names', f.51. Item 6: 'Cipher designed by Charles I., with note by the same. Holograph', f.53. Item 7: 'The names of severall persons knowne to King Charles the First of blessed memory by the letters of the alphabet heereafter mentioned who were serviceable to his majestic in the tymes of his most strickt ymprisonment by the Rebells in Ao 1648', in Firebrace's hand, f.54.
records_examined.relevance: HIGHEST - same 'J.' signature as the unsolved letters; holograph cipher (f.53) may be 'The Cypher' nomenclator itself; f.51 enclosure with 'cipher of names' on back is the same enclosure pattern as the 5 May letter
records_examined.title: ORIGINAL letters from Charles I., when prisoner in Carisbrooke Castle, Isle of Wight, to Henry Firebrace [afterwards knighted by Charles II.], relative to plans for his escape, the means of communication with his adherents, etc . ; 23 Apr.-27 Dec. 1648, and n.d. Holograph, in a feigned hand; signed "J." and addressed "D."

records_examined.extent: 70 photocopies (RP = Copies of Exported Manuscripts Deposited under Government Export Regulations; originals exported, current location unknown)
records_examined.relevance: HIGH - 66 secret IoW letters; published quotes from the Hopkins correspondence contain in-clear figure assignments (39/40, 47->52, 58, 64=Treaty, 715=Whorwood, 457=Lady Carliffe, 546/193, 714=Dr Fraizer; letter codes L=Osborne, W=Titus, N=Whorwood)
records_examined.scope: CHARLES I, King of England, Scotland, and Ireland. HOPKINS, George. Manuscript volume containing a transcript of the text of a Petition made to Charles II by Hopkins, (resident in Ireland) of Newport, Isle of Wight to redeem a promise made to him by that king to restore the family assets and estate which had to be sold to cover the cost of keeping and entertaining Charles I and his Court at the family home near Newport, Isle of Wight whilst he was negotiating the Treaty of Newport in 1648. Together with a copy of 66 secret letters written by Charles I and smuggled out of the Isle of Wight, the originals of which went into the hands of Hopkins. Ireland. Creation dates: Early 18th century

records_examined.relevance: MEDIUM - 18th-century copies; the f.80 cipher's system is unidentified (could be Hammond-correspondence cipher, not necessarily 'The Cypher')
records_examined.scope: 'LETTERS BETWEEN COL. ROBERT HAMMOND, Governor of the Isle of Wight, and the Committee ... at Derby House ... relating to Charles I ... in Carisbrooke Castle ...'; 1647, 1648. As prepared for the press by Birch, and printed with the above title in 1764 ... (f) a cipher. f. 80.
